sources.title: Guido W. Imbens and Joshua D. Angrist — Identification and Estimation of Local Average Treatment Effects
sources.version: Econometrica62(2), March1994, printed467–475; nine-page publisher scan hosted by Stanford GSB.
sources.inspection: Fresh public curl download; actual nine local page images rendered and individually visually read, physical1–9/printed467–475. All introduction, assumptions, Theorem1 proof, weighting/asymptotic statements, appendix proofs and references read; bibliography is not inspection of cited studies.
sources.use: Actual research reading in seminar: required Sections1–2/467–470 and Section4/472; binary compliance reconstruction and distinction between local and population targets. General weighting/asymptotic proofs are optional extension and not claimed taught in full.
sources.limits: No empirical application verification, fresh reading of cited underlying studies, current dataset access or institutional endorsement. No reproduction of source examples. Randomization alone does not establish exclusion; ratio requires nonzero first stage; estimated-instrument inference needs its own nuisance accounting.

sources.title: Alexander Balke and Judea Pearl — Bounds on Treatment Effects from Studies with Imperfect Compliance (UCLA repository manuscript marked To appear in JASA)
sources.version: Eleven physical pages: repository cover plus ten printed manuscript pages. Cover deposit date2011-10-25 is not treated as publication year; no draft/final identity asserted.
sources.inspection: Actual web-tool PDF body text read across eleven pages. Adopted bounded scope: Section1/printed1, Section2/printed2–3, start of Section3 response-type strategy/printed4, Section5/printed9. Detailed formulas/application passages returned corrupted mathematical text; no complete equation or empirical audit claimed. Two screenshot attempts failed; curl downloads returned empty files, so no local PDF/image inspection claimed.
sources.use: Actual research reading: population-effect target, maintained exclusion/random assignment setup, and stated policy objection to an instrument-dependent local target. Seminar asks whether that objection applies to the particular intervention; it does not declare the LATE theorem refuted.
sources.limits: No copying/general verification of the eight-term bounds or clinical application numbers; source sharpness/computation follows a more general response-type model beyond chapter proof. The paper explicitly retains exclusion and random-assignment assumptions: no assumption-free guarantee adopted. Paper references later Angrist–Imbens–Rubin1996; R1 is the earlier foundation, not a claimed direct reply. No medical or current policy guidance.
sources.access: Web primary repository body accessible in actual retrieval; local-download/image routes unsuccessful. Instructor must arrange lawful participant access before launch.

selection: Purposive two-paper identification/target sequence, not comprehensive literature or novelty certification. An initially considered Manski1990 route returned an access challenge; it is not a completed assigned primary reading.
original_material: All syllabus arrangements, type populations, bounds inputs, proofs, questions, memos, proposal, feedback, exercises and solutions are original synthetic instruction. No source numerical examples or actual learner outcomes copied.
runtime: Exactly four author files. Source PDFs and retained evidence are provenance only, not runtime dependencies.
